source_text: καὶ ταῦτα γράφομεν ⸀ἡμεῖς ἵνα ἡ χαρὰ ἡμῶν ᾖ πεπληρωμένη.
english_snapshot: And we are writing these things so that our joy may be complete[a].

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'your joy' instead of 'our joy.'

source_text: καὶ ὑμεῖς χρῖσμα ἔχετε ἀπὸ τοῦ ἁγίου ⸀καὶ οἴδατε ⸀πάντες·
english_snapshot: But you have an anointing from the Holy One[a], and you all know.

signals.text: Or, in another textual reading, 'and you know all things.' The SBLGNT reading supports 'and you all know.'

source_text: πᾶς ὁ ἀρνούμενος τὸν υἱὸν οὐδὲ τὸν πατέρα ἔχει· ⸂ὁ ὁμολογῶν τὸν υἱὸν καὶ τὸν πατέρα ἔχει⸃.
english_snapshot: Everyone who denies the Son does not have the Father either[a]; whoever confesses the Son has the Father also.

signals.text: Some manuscripts omit: 'whoever confesses the Son has the Father also.'

source_text: καὶ ὑμεῖς τὸ χρῖσμα ὃ ἐλάβετε ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ ⸂μένει ἐν ὑμῖν⸃, καὶ οὐ χρείαν ἔχετε ἵνα τις διδάσκῃ ὑμᾶς· ἀλλ’ ὡς τὸ ⸀αὐτοῦ χρῖσμα διδάσκει ὑμᾶς περὶ πάντων, καὶ ἀληθές ἐστιν καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν ψεῦδος, καὶ καθὼς ἐδίδαξεν ὑμᾶς, ⸀μένετε ἐν αὐτῷ.
english_snapshot: And as for you[a], the anointing that you received from him remains in you, and you have no need that anyone should teach you. But as his anointing teaches you about all things, and is true and is not a lie, and just as it taught you[b], remain in him.

signals.text: Or, in some manuscripts, 'and just as it taught you, you remain in him.'

source_text: ἴδετε ποταπὴν ἀγάπην δέδωκεν ἡμῖν ὁ πατὴρ ἵνα τέκνα θεοῦ κληθῶμεν, ⸂καὶ ἐσμέν⸃. διὰ τοῦτο ὁ κόσμος οὐ γινώσκει ⸀ἡμᾶς ὅτι οὐκ ἔγνω αὐτόν.
english_snapshot: See what kind of love the Father has given to us[a], that we should be called children of God—and we are. For this reason the world does not know us[e][d][c][b], because it did not know him.

source_text: καὶ πᾶν πνεῦμα ὃ μὴ ὁμολογεῖ ⸀τὸν ⸀Ἰησοῦν ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ οὐκ ἔστιν· καὶ τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ τοῦ ἀντιχρίστου, ὃ ἀκηκόατε ὅτι ἔρχεται, καὶ νῦν ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ ἐστὶν ἤδη.
english_snapshot: and every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not from God[a]. And this is the spirit of the antichrist, which you have heard is coming[c][b], and now is already in the world.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read, 'does not confess that Jesus Messiah has come in the flesh.'

source_text: ἡμεῖς ⸀ἀγαπῶμεν, ὅτι αὐτὸς πρῶτος ἠγάπησεν ἡμᾶς.
english_snapshot: We love because he first loved us[a].

signals.text: Some manuscripts read, 'We love him because he first loved us.'

english_snapshot: For there are three who testify,[a]

signals.text: Later manuscripts add a longer reading often known as the Comma Johanneum: 'in heaven: the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit, and these three are one. And there are three that bear witness on earth ...' This wording is absent from the earliest Greek manuscript evidence and is not included in the SBLGNT text.

source_text: ὁ πιστεύων εἰς τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ ἔχει τὴν μαρτυρίαν ἐν ⸀αὑτῷ· ὁ μὴ πιστεύων τῷ θεῷ ψεύστην πεποίηκεν αὐτόν, ὅτι οὐ πεπίστευκεν εἰς τὴν μαρτυρίαν ἣν μεμαρτύρηκεν ὁ θεὸς περὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ.
english_snapshot: The one who believes in the Son of God has the testimony in himself[a]; the one who does not believe God has made him a liar[b], because he has not believed the testimony that God has testified about his Son.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'in him' instead of 'in himself,' which could be understood as 'in the Son' rather than 'in himself.'
